title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: V is a real vector space of dimension 2 and V_C is its complexification. Complex lines L ⊂ V_C are the points of Σ = P(V)(C) ≅ P^1(C). The previous page shows that L defines a complex structure on V exactly when Re: L → V is an isomorphism, i.e. L ∩ V = 0, i.e. L is not the complexification of a real line, i.e. z ∉ Σ_R = P(V)(R) ≅ P^1(R).

This page finishes the argument.
(1) Complex structures J on V are in bijection with Σ∖Σ_R. In modern terms, J corresponds to one of its ±i-eigenlines in V_C; the margin of the previous page worries about which of L_ω or its conjugate to choose.
(2) Σ∖Σ_R = P^1(C)∖P^1(R) has two connected components, the two open hemispheres or discs, labelled Σ*_ω. Each disc induces a boundary orientation on the circle Σ_R; this is what 'par Stokes' means. So the components correspond to the two orientations of Σ_R, equivalently of V. The component containing z is the one whose orientation agrees with the orientation that the complex structure J_z induces on V (the basis (v, J_z v) is positive).
(3) Transcendental description of complex elliptic curves. E amounts to the following data:
- (a) a free Z-module Π of rank 2 (marginally, Π = π_1(E, 0_E) = H_1(E, Z));
- (b) an orientation ω of V = Π⊗R ≅ t_E (Lie algebra / tangent space at the origin, via the exponential uniformisation), equivalently a generator of Λ^2_Z Π, equivalently a reduction of the structure group GL(2,Z) to SL(2,Z);
- (c) a point z of the component Σ*_ω(V), which fixes the complex structure on V compatible with ω.
Then E = V/Π with that complex structure.
(4) Torelli rigidification (definition begun here, finished on the next page): an orientation-preserving isomorphism Z^2 → Π, i.e. an oriented basis (z_1, z_2) with z_1 ∧ z_2 = ω. This identifies Σ*_ω with the Poincaré half-plane D. Rigidified curves then correspond to points of D, and SL(2,Z) acts on the rigidifications, recovering the moduli SL(2,Z)\D.

The purpose is to set up the classical analytic model of the moduli of elliptic curves (level structures and the action of SL(2,Z) on the upper half-plane). Presumably this serves as a comparison with the algebraic/stack-theoretic study of the moduli in characteristic ≠ 2 in this dossier, and with the fundamental group of the moduli stack, SL(2,Z), relevant to the anabelian/Teichmüller themes of 1980–82.
errors: No mathematical error. Sign and convention issues are left open: whether a complex structure should correspond to L or its conjugate (previous page's margin), and which half-plane D^+ or D^- corresponds to the standard orientation (next page's insertion). The marginal note on this page asks for something to be checked, very likely this sign. These are conventions, not errors.

Minor redundancy: the orientation ω in (b) is determined by z in (c), since z ∈ Σ∖Σ_R already fixes the component. Including ω is a deliberate bookkeeping choice that reduces the structure group to SL(2,Z), not a mistake.
In item (c), Σ_ω(V) should read Σ*_ω(V), the component, as on the next page.

ideas.what: Complex structures on a real 2-plane V correspond to points of P(V)(C)∖P(V)(R) via (anti)holomorphic eigenlines in V_C
ideas.modern_name: Period domain for weight-1 Hodge structures of rank 2 / P^1(C)∖P^1(R) = two copies of the upper half-plane

ideas.what: The two components of P^1(C)∖P^1(R) correspond to the two orientations of P^1(R) and of V (boundary orientation, 'Stokes')
Complex elliptic curve = (rank-2 lattice Π = π_1(E), orientation of Π⊗R, compatible complex structure); V ≅ t_E
'Rigidification de Torelli' = oriented basis Z^2 ≅ Π, with SL(2,Z) acting by change of basis
ideas.modern_name: Framing/marking of an elliptic curve; Teichmüller space D with mapping class group SL(2,Z)
ideas.where_published: The terminology 'rigidification' is Grothendieck-style; Teichmüller towers appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this specific term is not known to me in print

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but entirely classical account of complex structures on R^2, the half-plane D, and marked elliptic curves. The only distinctive feature is Grothendieck's terminology ('rigidification de Torelli'), together with his attention to orientation and sign conventions. There is no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Item (c): the symbol is Σ_ω(V), meant as Σ*_ω(V) (the star is not clearly visible here, but the next page uses Σ*_{V,ω}).
The insertion 'Σ*_ω' above 'composantes connexes' labels the components; read 'deux composantes connexes Σ*_ω'.

The left margin note beside the paragraph on the component of z is hard to read. The machine reading 'Vérifier point de colonne vers le bas' is doubtful; it is likely an instruction to verify the sign/orientation convention ('Vérifier ... vers le bas').
The margin reads 'on a Π = π_1(E, 0_E), V = Π⊗_Z R ≃ t_E'; the letter is Π throughout. The next page's transcription writes H for the same module.
